Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

correct verb

put right a mistake

also correction, put right, correct someone, mark homework

classical

Hor. Ars 438: corrige, sōdēs, hoc
Quint. 1.1.11: corrigat prōtinus
Cic. Att. 2.7.5: mendum nōs corrigēmus
Traupman 27, 29

corrigō, corrigere, corrēxī, corrēctum

verb, third conjugation

correct, put right

To straighten what has gone crooked: a mistake (mendum, peccātum, errōrem corrigere), a text, a person. Traupman: of a person or of a mistake (p. 29).

Other words

  • ēmendō, ēmendāre, ēmendāvī, ēmendātum — correct (a text, a piece of work), free from mistakes

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Quint. 2.2.5: quae ēmendanda erunt; Traupman 29, 246

    Of written work: the teacher corrects his pupils’ writing (ut scrīptūram vestram ēmendem, Vives, Exerc. 10); see also improve. Correction is ēmendātiō or corrēctiō (Traupman 29).

Examples

  • Quīntiliō sī quid recitārēs, «corrige, sōdēs, hoc» ajēbat «et hoc».

    If you read anything out to Quintilius, he would say, “Correct this, please, and this.”Hor. Ars 438–439

  • at ūnus certē sit assiduus loquendī nōn imperītus, quī, sī qua erunt ab hīs praesente alumnō dicta vitiōsē, corrigat prōtinus nec īnsīdere illī sinat

    at least let there be one person always at hand who speaks well, to correct at once anything the others say wrongly in the child’s hearing, and not let it settle in himQuint. 1.1.11

See also mistake, improve, grade, correct, homework.
